reading: The listing line is the most finished SYSTEM the tournament has made: slate bands with a head column, one-line rows read along a leader to tabular facts, steel reverse video for "here", denim links, a figure over a caps label in every head column, WHO/DUE column heads, a NOW divider, 0 small targets. Usability, interaction and system have scored it 8+ for four rounds, and no lens ever attacked its grammar. What sank it from #1 (r11) to #2 (r12) to #6 (r13) was not a flaw but a fading: "a known quantity", "a refined admin listing more than a memorable mood" (style 6.9), "quieter in CRT character and line art than the leaders", "below the fold mostly a matte listing" (soul), "the wide head column reads a bit like an admin page" (feedback), "the Home hero is crowded and the box sits mid-hero" (style, interaction). Its unfixed finish faults have been named for two rounds by nearly every lens: the Next up trace reads as a barcode, the Ideas radar is squeezed into a 212px portrait tube (now pushed to the column's foot), Coming up prints the date twice ('9 OCT FRI' beside 'Friday 9 October'), the hover afterglow on a setup row is an amber-bronze fill that reads as selected (skeptic in r12 and r13), Status's 44rem measure leaves 230px of dead band, Ideas still mixes one-tap kind keys with Status/For selects behind a Filter button, To do's search is cut off with an icon-only button, Status draws "off" as a red ring (an alarm), and it still carries "What's on your mind?", the title the owner rejected. What would make it win: keep the listing whole and make it LIT and LESS ADMIN. The tour finals have exactly the features it lacks: Sill Line's tube that drops a lit line into Coming up (feedback 9.1, "the best single gesture on the panel"), Lit Manual's round phosphor dials ("the most beautiful new tubes on the panel"), Settled Light's household index row ("the best whole-service idea here; the main tournament should adopt it"), plus the one row afterglow that ever registered in a capture (L228). Those put phosphor below the fold where it means something, take the greeting from crowded to one gesture, and turn the head column from an admin sidebar into a listing's channel column.

briefs.name: Listing, Lit Through
briefs.hypothesis: Evening Listing, Traced lost ground only on mood and light, never on its system. This cross keeps every structural win (band + head column, leader rows to tabular facts, figure over label, column heads, NOW divider, steel 'here', 0 small targets) and spends the change where its judges said it was flat: one lit gesture that runs from the greeting's tube down into Coming up (Sill Line), a lit round dial heading Plans and Status so phosphor lives below the fold on real data (Lit Manual), and a household index band that ends Home as a listing's 'also on' (Settled Light). With the two-round backlog of finish faults cleared, it should read as the calm, complete standard AND as a lit programme guide, beating its carried parent on soul, style and feedback without giving back usability or system.
briefs.brief: Start from r12-idea-1's files (palettes/r12-idea-1.json, variants/r12-idea-1/{build.py,palette.css,templates/}). Keep the palette tokens (bg #0b0e0c, surface #151b1e, steel accent #84a0c4, denim links, bone ink #d4cfc4, heading #ebe6da, lit sage #86d9a6, brand/screen exactly #6dff9c, screenGlow 1.0, glow 0.9), the condensed Instrument Sans heads, Plex body, Plex Mono for figures only, VT323 on glass only, the tuning scale under the bar, the bar in words. TYPE SYSTEM (write as tokens at the top of palette.css and use nowhere else): --t-display 2.75rem/1.05 (the greeting title only), --t-h1 2.5rem (page titles), --t-figure 2.25rem Plex Sans 300 tabular-nums (head-column numerals), --t-band 1.375rem condensed 600 (band heads), --t-row 1rem 600 (row names), --t-fact .9375rem Plex Mono tabular (facts), --t-body .9375rem, --t-label .8125rem (13px floor; caps labels +.06em tracking, sentence-case for every control and link). Three rule weights: --rule-band 1px var(--line-2) (band top), --rule-row 1px dotted var(--line-2) (leaders), --rule-col 1px var(--line) (column heads). Head-column numeral sits on the same baseline as the first row's name (align via grid row 1 + align-self:baseline). THE BAND (all pages): .band loses its slate panel fill; the band is page ground with a single --rule-band top rule. Rows (.row) keep their slate strip (surface) so the family's things are the solid objects and the head column reads as a programme guide's channel column, not an admin sidebar. Head column narrows to 13rem (.band-head width) and holds only: icon + band head, the figure over its caps label, at most two state links ('3 late →', 'All 4 →'), and the band's one-tap keys where it filters. Every explanatory sentence that sat in a head column ('Google Calendar is not connected, so these are the plans the bot made', setup's 'Each one is a short page…', Settings' long note) moves to a .band-foot line under the rows at --t-label in --dim, one line, full row measure. HOME, top to bottom: 1. Greeting (.welcome). Drop the left identity column (Vera's screen tile, 'Vera', 'FRI 2 OCT' that wrapped). In its place a dateline above the title: her 28px screen tile, 'Vera' 600, then 'Friday 2 October' in --dim, one line, nowrap. Title .ask-question at --t-display, full ink #ebe6da: 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (full stop inside the lit run). 'line up.' carries the kit's E1 two-layer halo with a white-hot core (text-shadow 0 0 1px #eafff1, 0 0 6px #6dff9c, 0 0 18px rgb(109 255 156/.45)). Box under the title at full width of the left column: E4 halo ring, turning #6dff9c while someone writes (:focus-within), E7 pool + scanlines rising from under Send (keep the parent's pool). Send stays on the From row. Starters: three stacked full-width keys under the box on the phone, a single row on desktop, each saying where it usually lands at the right in --dim ('usually Plans', 'usually To do', 'usually Ideas', Platformed's device rebuilt in steel, no colour fills). Right column: the Next up tube (see 3). The greeting ends at the box's foot; nothing else sits in it. 2. The lit stem (graft A). From the Next up tube's foot a 2px #6dff9c line with a white-hot 1px core drops through the gap, turns left along Coming up's band top rule and arrives at the NOW lamp at the top of Coming up's rail, which then lights only the stretch from NOW to the first row's ring; the rest of the rail stays steel. The tube's plan is that first stop: Coming up's first row is the Next up plan, flagged 'Next' in sage, so tube and list are one thing. Once per load the run draws itself (Sill's route-sets-on-opening, 600ms, prefers-reduced-motion: none). Below 64rem the stem turns down the left gutter from beside the tube (Sill's phone rule). 3. Next up tube (fixing the barcode): keep the tube, its scope and words, but redraw the four-week trace at ~2x height: pulses 3 units wide and 60% of the trace's height, weekends as a faint shaded band, the next pulse labelled on the glass ('Sun 4 · roller rink'), a one-line key under the glass in --t-label ('a bar is a plan · weekends shaded'), each bar a link to its plan (aria-label with the plan's name). Tube align-self:start and sized to its content: no empty glass. 4. Coming up band (moved directly under the greeting so the stem lands uninterrupted). Head column: '4 / PLANS', 'next in 2 days' only if not echoed by row 1 (drop it), 'All plans →'. Rows: rail ring, the day chip ('9' + 'OCT/FRI' stacked), name, leader, then time (Plex Mono) and relative ('in 7 days'). DELETE the long 'Friday 9 October' sub-column. Calendar note → .band-foot. 5. Setup strip (graft A's setup strip, rebuilt): replaces the three-row setup band. One line: a 2px amber left edge on a slate body (no amber fill, no amber rings), 'Finish setting up' at --t-band in heading ink, '3 left' with the 3 as an amber tabular figure, three 28px steel step rings on a short line with the next one rimmed in #6dff9c, 'Next: choose your own password →' as the one denim link, 'All 3 steps' at the right. The whole strip is a 48px row; on the phone two lines max. 6. To do band: unchanged grammar (head '4 / OPEN', '3 late →' amber link to ?late=1, 'All 4 →'; WHO/DUE heads; NOW divider). Checkboxes are neutral steel squares for every row; late is amber WORDS only ('was due 5 days ago'), never an amber box outline. Fix the after-NOW row so its checkbox sits on the same x as the rows above (one grid column for the tick, the NOW divider spanning columns 2-end). 7. Lately added band: keep (KIND/FOR/# heads, two-up kind tint wells). 'Something to eat · 2 restaurants to try →' becomes its last row, not a separate card. 8. Also on (graft C): the last band, head 'Also on' with no figure, rows in the listing grammar, one per page outside the main five: Wishes (leader → 'Maya 0 · Theo 0 open', each name a link), Memory ('Tell Vera something →'), Family ('4 people'), Status ('1 of 3 on' plus three 8px lamps in the status code below), Settings ('9 parts'). Each row a 48px link target with the page's icon in its tint well. Replaces the kids' wishes band and the 'Something to eat' card. IDEAS: page head row: title + description left, primary 'Add an idea' under the description (one green primary); right of the head, the radar in a 4:3 landscape tube (~22rem x 16.5rem) with its words BESIDE the scope in VT323 ('10 places from home', 'Nearest #7 Pumpkin patch · 18 min NW', 'Furthest #4 Cannon Beach'), no wrapping at 17 characters. Head column (13rem): '12 / IDEAS', then three one-tap key groups, each a 2-up grid of 44px latched keys with steel reverse for the chosen: Kind (All + nine kinds), For (Anyone, Sam, Alex, Maya, Theo), Status (Open, Done, Dropped, Any). Delete the Status and For selects and the Filter button. Main column: one search field at full width with a worded 'Search' button, then 'Save a thought for later' fold, then the list with KIND/DRIVE/WAY/FOR/# heads. TO DO: head column '4 / OPEN', '3 late →', then Open / Late / Done / Cancelled / All as latched keys (Late new, ?late=1). Main column: search at full width at the top with a worded 'Search' button (placeholder visible: 'dentist, library…'), then 'Add something to do', then the rows. Row action says 'Edit or snooze' (pencil + words, regular weight). PLANS (list and month), graft B: the head column opens on a round phosphor dial: a 11rem round tube in the listing's thin grooved graphite bezel (no graph-paper grid, no 'Fig.' caption), VT323 at full ink 'Next in / 2 days / then 3 more', a ring of 28 day ticks around it with now at 12 o'clock, a lit #6dff9c tick on each day with a plan, steel ticks otherwise, the tube's bloom, scanlines and breathing power lamp. Under it the List / Month keys and '5 / PLANS IN OCTOBER'. Month: today's cell keeps a steel reverse numeral plus one lit outline; no per-week rails. List: rail lit only from NOW to the next plan. STATUS, graft B again + lamp code: the first band is 'What it costs': its head column holds the round cost dial (same component: '$0.00 / of $2.00 / today' in VT323, a needle or lit arc for the day's share, a ghost tick at the limit), and its rows the cost breakdown. Then Who answers, Keys, Connected to: rows run the full band measure (drop the 44rem cap), set two-up where rows are short (Keys already is; make Connected to two-up at >=72rem). One lamp family, one meaning each, with a legend under the first head column ('What a lamp says'): working = #6dff9c dot with a two-layer halo that breathes while the dot stays lit; waiting = steel dot; off or not set up = pewter ring (#66727a), NOT red; needs a look = amber ring with an amber core; red only when something has stopped. Who answers keeps its rail lit lamp to lamp. SETTINGS, FORM, CHAT: inherit the band (no panel fill, top rule, 13rem head column, prose to .band-foot), the type tokens, the lamp code and the afterglow. Chat keeps the timetable rail ending in the lit ring at the box. ROW AFTERGLOW (graft D, every .row, task row, idea row, Also-on row, settings card): on :hover and :has(:focus-visible) a 12% steel wash (--row-wash: rgb(132 160 196/.12)), a 2px inset sage edge (inset 2px 0 0 #86d9a6) and a short halo (0 0 18px -10px #86d9a6), on in .12s, decaying over 1.4s cubic-bezier(.25,.45,.35,1). Never amber or bronze, so a hovered setup row cannot read as selected. LIGHT LIST (everything else matte): the mark, 'line up.', the box while written in, Send, the stem and the NOW-to-next stretch, NOW lamps, the Next up tube, the radar, the two dials, working status lamps, focus rings. Each tube gets the kit's power-on from a line (scale(1,.01) brightness 3 → 1.03 → 1, 450ms, once per load). Update STYLE.md notes in removed.txt: the type tokens, the rule weights, the lamp code, the light list.
briefs.borrows:
Its own judges' fixes, most-cited first: (1) the Next up trace reads as a barcode: taller pulses, the next one labelled on the glass, a key, bars as links (feedback, soul, system, interaction, usability, skeptic r12). (2) Coming up's repeated long date: drop 'Friday 9 October', keep chip, time, relative (system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic r12). (3) The 212px portrait radar on Ideas: a 4:3 landscape tube with words beside the scope (feedback, soul, system, usability, skeptic r12; usability r13 'pushed to the foot'). (4) The amber-bronze hover reading as selected: a steel wash with a sage edge, decaying (system, interaction, skeptic, usability r12; skeptic r13). (5) Status's 44rem measure / 230px dead band: full measure, two-up, a dial in the head column (feedback, system, type r12). (6) Ideas mixes one-tap kinds with Status/For selects: all three as one-tap keys in the head column, selects and Filter dropped (usability r12, r13). (7) Head-column prose wrapping to five lines: moved to a band foot line (type r12). (8) To do's squeezed search: full width with a worded button (interaction r12). (9) 'Edit' → 'Edit or snooze' (interaction, usability r12). (10) the After-NOW checkbox offset (interaction r13). (11) the crowded hero with the box mid-hero and the wide 'admin' head column (style, interaction, feedback r13). (12) light below the fold (soul r11-r13, feedback r13).

briefs.avoids: 'A known quantity / refined admin listing' (style, system, feedback r13): the band loses its slate panel and becomes ground plus a top rule, the head column narrows and sheds its prose, and three new lit things (stem, two dials) change the content, not a corner. 'Wash in the corner' (owner, skeptic on Afterglow): no page-head haze; every new light draws data (the plan's day, days to next, the day's spend). 'Below the fold mostly matte' (soul): the stem, the lit NOW stretch, the Plans and Status dials and the breathing lamps carry phosphor down the page. 'Home hero crowded, box mid-hero' (style, interaction r13): the identity column goes, the title sits over the box, the tube stands alone at the right. The barcode trace, the portrait radar, the repeated date, the bronze hover, the dead Status band, the mixed filter mechanisms, the cut-off search, the red off-rings and the amber-outlined checkboxes are all removed. The tour's failures are avoided too: no rails beyond their order (only NOW-to-next is lit; no week rails on the month), no amber slabs or rings, no inverted-green chips, no sideways-scrolling starters, no invented clock times, no graph-paper or Fig. costume. What it gives up to make room: Vera's identity column in the greeting (now a dateline), the long-date sub-column, the three-row setup band, the separate kids' wishes band and Something to eat card (both folded into rows), the Ideas portrait tube in the head column, the Status/For selects and Filter button, and the slate fill behind every band.
briefs.title: Tell Vera what to *line up*. Not yet tried. It keeps the imperative form that won every note in the tour's last round ('Tell Vera what to plan.': it names who hears you and invites a message rather than asking to be shown something), and puts the lineage's own word on the lit run. A programme listing is the evening's line-up, and 'line up' is what the family does with Vera: a weekend, a reminder, an idea kept for later, a wish. It cannot be answered 'no', it does not presume a plan exists, and the lit word falls at the end of the line, with the full stop inside the lit run. Its predecessor 'What shall we line up?' was faulted for a formal 'shall' and for lighting a word that named the design's motif rather than the job. This version drops 'shall', and on a listing page 'line up' is the job. It is seven lit characters, under the eight-letter halo limit. If the judges hear a queue, 'Tell Vera what to plan.' remains this line's fallback.
